deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 27% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 31% last year; 19%/yr over 3 years — roughly in line with its recent growth.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 6% (3 years ago -1%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $6 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 14% (3 years ago -2%). (Tax rate estimated at 21%: effective rate not reported.)

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $64M, up 100% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Receivables (money customers still owe) up 53% vs quarterly sales up 37% (days to collect 66 → 74). Customers may be paying more slowly, or sales were pulled forward.
Profit leans on non-operating gains: net income $2.6B vs operating income $1.6B over the last 12 months (e.g. investment gains or one-offs that may not repeat).

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 19%/yr over 3 years and 22%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 17% vs a 5-year range of -18–17% (median -4%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).
deeper.margin_position: near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back)

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $2.1B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($1.9B buybacks + $209M dividends) = 1.4% of the company's market value. Share count up 5.8% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $7.35, up 18% in 90 days (up 1% in the last 30); 27 analysts raised, 1 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $4.22, up 4% in 90 days; 7 analysts raised, 1 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By product, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Data center 79% of sales, up 46%; Communications and other 21% of sales, up 10%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 4 quarters running by about 1%: beating is now expected, so a small beat may not lift the stock.

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.sub: latest quarter +37% vs a year earlier · 12-month sales $9.5B
tiles.read: Latest quarter: sales up 37% vs a year earlier and speeding up (from 22% two quarters ago): demand is strengthening.
tiles.explain: Headline: sales over the last 12 months vs the 12 months before. Bars: each quarter's sales vs the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $17 of operating profit, up from $1 a year ago: profitability is improving.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Only 66% of reported profit became spare cash, usually because of heavy investment; worth watching.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 56× last year's profit (higher than 50% of the last 5 years); only 23× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings

tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.
